To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
women's perceptions of discrimination against the group women are related to their views of themselves and the group, and these are, in turn, related to their psychological distress.

perceptions of discrimination against all women (public and private collective self-esteem), perceptions of discrimination against one-self (personal self-esteem), and the interaction of public and private collective self esteem with perceptions of discrimination against the self (public collective self-esteem x personal self-esteem) are associated with women's psychological distress (depression and anxiety).

women who perceive discrimination against them have lower levels of both collective and personal self esteem, and that these lower levels of self-esteem mediate the relation between perceived discrimination and psychological distress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a social problem that has received little attention in psychology: the effects of discrimination against women on women's mental health.
the effects of discrimination against women on the psychological well-being of women.
the impact of discrimination on women's well-being.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study are not consistent with the feminist theory that discrimination is a cause of women's psychological distress.

the results of the present study indicate that perceptions of discrimination against females are related to psychological distress, and that this effect is mediated by both collective and personal self esteem.
the more discrimination women experience, the more they feel that the group women is inferior, which in turn makes women feel less valued as individuals and more distressed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the experience of discrimination is harmful to women, and this harm is mediated in part by negative appraisals of the group to which one belongs and of oneself as a person.
women who experience discrimination may be harmed in part by the negative effects of discrimination on both their views of women as a group and on their views of themselves.
perceptions of discrimination against one's group may be harmful to one's psychological well-being.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of discrimination are not only personal, but they are also group-based and can be ameliorated by group-based efforts to improve self-esteem and psychological well-being.

women's psychological distress is not simply a function of how often they are personally discriminated against, but is also a function of how they view the group women and how they view themselves as individuals.
perceptions of discrimination against one's own group are associated with negative outcomes, and this is especially so when the group to which one belongs is stigmatized and devalued.
